passage: Vinita had spent three weeks scanning receipts and refilling the pantry at a small architecture studio, and her stipend barely covered her train fare. Rain hammered the windows the day she carried the fifth carton of files upstairs. She wanted to learn drafting. "Tejas sir, could I sit with the drawings team on Thursday? And could you tell me what I'm expected to learn here by the end of this month?" Tejas blinked, then admitted that the last intern never asked. "Try the site sketches. Show me on Friday." Vinita nodded and wrote it down. She decided that if she was still only carrying cartons at the end of the month, she would look for another internship.

qa.q: How many weeks had Vinita spent scanning receipts and refilling the pantry?
qa.a: She had spent three weeks doing it.

qa.q: How did Vinita feel about her internship by the fifth carton, and what did she want?
qa.a: She was likely frustrated, with a stipend that barely covered her fare and only cartons to carry, and she wanted to learn drafting.

qa.q: What could Vinita do if the work does not change by the end of the month?
qa.a: Look for another internship, as she decided, since she asked for a clear role and feedback first.

qa.q: How might Tejas see Vinita's questions?
qa.a: Tejas blinked and admitted the last intern never asked, so the questions may have shown that the role had been left vague. 🙂

grounding: An intern given menial work with no learning asks for a clear role and feedback and decides when to move on.

passage:
Note from the internship coordinator, law firm placement, week 5
I visited the firm today for Dilnaz's mid-internship review. She has spent five weeks photocopying, filing and fetching lunch for the associate she reports to, Trisha. She has not been to court once or drafted a single document. In the break room, she told me quietly that she felt "useless" and too embarrassed to tell her parents what she does all day.
I suggested she request a defined role, in writing. We drafted three lines together: what she hopes to learn, one task she would like to try, and a request for fifteen minutes of feedback each Friday.
She sent it to Trisha before I left. Trisha replied within the hour, apologising: she had been swamped and had not planned for an intern. Dilnaz will attend a hearing on Tuesday and draft a notice.
If nothing changes in two weeks, I have told Dilnaz we can discuss moving her to another placement.

qa.q: How many weeks had Dilnaz spent photocopying and filing?
How did Dilnaz feel about her internship?
qa.a: Useless, and too embarrassed to tell her parents what she did all day.

qa.q: What did the coordinator help Dilnaz ask for?
qa.a: A clear role in writing: what she hopes to learn, one task to try, and fifteen minutes of feedback each Friday.

qa.q: Why had Trisha given Dilnaz only menial tasks?
qa.a: She had been swamped and hadn't planned for an intern, and she apologised quickly.

grounding: Shows an intern given only menial work, and asking for a clear role and feedback, with a plan to move on if nothing changes.

passage:
Thursday
Week 7 of the internship. Today's big task: arranging chairs for Amandeep's investor meeting and ordering samosas. Yesterday: a spreadsheet of the office's printer ink.
I finally did the thing I'd been putting off. I asked Amandeep for ten minutes and said, "I'm grateful for the internship, but I'm not learning anything about marketing. Could I shadow one campaign, or get one real task a week?"
He said, "Sure, sure, next week," without looking up. That's what he said in week 3 and week 5.
I've written down everything I've been given since week 1. It's all errands. I also asked for feedback and got "you're doing great", which means nothing.
So I've decided: if nothing changes by next Friday, I'll leave politely at the end of the month and apply for the agency internship Pooja from college mentioned. I'm not going to keep smiling and ordering samosas.
— Vaibhav

qa.a: Arranging chairs for Amandeep's investor meeting and ordering samosas.

qa.q: How does Vaibhav feel about the internship by week 7?
qa.a: Frustrated and stuck, tired of errands and empty "next week" promises.

qa.q: How did Vaibhav act instead of silently accepting it?
qa.a: Asked clearly for a real task, asked for feedback, listed every errand, and set a date to leave politely if nothing changes.

qa.q: How does Amandeep seem to see the intern?
qa.a: As a helper for errands; he says "Sure, sure, next week" without even looking up.

grounding: Illustrates an internship with no learning, asking for a clear role and feedback, and deciding when to move on rather than silently accepting.
